title: Judaeo-Arabic jottings in an invented sign alphabet, Cairo Geniza, Cambridge University Library T-S NS J479

steps.what: PGP 8804 and Elbaum's 2022 blog post read: Elbaum has a tentative key and has read the alphabet, signature, two Burda verses, a legal phrase and an erotic passage; no full reading published.
Both sides fetched at full resolution (3097 x 4366, 3069 x 4319) by IIIF regions and stitched (stitch.py).
Alphabet row at the foot of side 2 read as 22 signs and labelled (glyph_chart.png); direction (right-to-left or left-to-right) not yet fixed.
Side 2 transcribed in shape labels by an agent (tr_side2.md): 351 signs, new variant labels a s 8 n 2 y h e t g z 5.

Key and direction found: the alphabet rows are the Hebrew alphabet left to right (I=alef ... 7=tav) and the scribe writes words and lines left to right. Variants a=tav, s=resh, 8=resh, e=het. Side 2 then reads the two Burda verses, the legal phrase jara dhalika fi akhir jumada al-tha[mi], and the word ksatban.

Side 1 transcribed in shape labels by an agent (tr_side1.md): 328 signs; under the key the signature al-faqir Ishaq al-yahudi, 'kull hadha kadhib', 'al-hamdu lillah rabb al-'alamin' and an erotic passage appear.

Elbaum's annotated photocopy checked after the key was found: it shows side 1 turned 180 degrees with Hebrew letters reading right to left; his legible readings agree with ours (kull hadha kadhib, al-qa'r, rahimha).

Two agents re-read every line in Hebrew letters under the key (tr_hebrew_side1.md, tr_hebrew_side2.md). Burda verses 1-2, the date formula, the signature, ksatban, a love-poetry line, al-hamdu lillah, and an erotic passage about Rahma ending 'my dove, all this is lies' read; seven rows (about 136 letters) give letters but no sense, mostly letter trials.
Burda verses 1-2 compared letter by letter with the standard text: the key gives them with only phonetic spellings and two slips; the scribe's alphabet rows confirm every sign value.
Side-1 alphabet row S1L14 puts the 7-sign in the bet slot and the loop-tail sign in the tsade/tav slots: a variant alphabet; with 7=bet the S1L04 verb reads wybk, the same verb as ybk in S1L02.

Hard rows: S1L03 is an alphabet row written upside down; the verb read as yabukk (Lisan al-Arab bkk, sexual sense) in S1L02 and S1L04; Rahma in S2L10; S1L10 a letter trial; slot comparison of 12 alphabet rows lists the variant signs. Elbaum's copy used as a check.
Date formula continues 'sanat ar[...]' (the year ending in 4 or a round x40) and stops against an alphabet row: no year survives.

Dating from formulary and vocabulary (dating_evidence.md): the petition pairing al-mawaqif al-'aliya + a'laha Allah ta'ala appears only in late Geniza petitions (c. 1600); 'jumada al-thani' is rare before the 15th century; Burda floor c. 1290-1365. Most likely c. 1400-1650 CE.

Orientation of every open row checked (tr_turned_rows.md): S1L07 written with the page turned (only 'hadha' reads); S1L08 letter practice; no new words. About 302 of 406 non-alphabet signs read (74%).

CTTS project: 46 bands, 682 candidate boxes, two blind labelling agents, aligned with the transcription (336 of 637 agreed), then every disagreement and missing sign decided on enlarged crops by two reviewers (167 type changes, 81 deletions, 3 merges, 15 splits, 129 additions, 103 marked uncertain). Written as CTTS project files (697 boxes, 84 types), not opened in CTTS; sign table of the 592 certain boxes drawn for the page. Model-made, not person-checked.

Second CTTS correction round after a line-by-line review of the sign table: 282 boxes in confused rows re-judged on enlarged crops (58 relabelled, 4 deleted, 17 split, 37 more marked uncertain). The cup U exists only on side 2; side-1 tailed loops moved from U to a; the 7 row mostly held plain strokes; s and 8 are one sign on side 2. Project now 711 boxes, 86 types, 140 uncertain; table 569 boxes. Model-made, not opened in CTTS, not person-checked.

Third CTTS correction round on the user's reading of the sign table: rows B, -, < each split into two shapes (B/Bc, -/J, </<5) and every row from f down re-judged (168 boxes). 12 deleted, f cut to 11 certain boxes. Project now 699 boxes, 83 types, 127 uncertain; table 570 boxes in 38 rows. Model-made, not opened in CTTS, not person-checked.

The owner went through the printed CTTS sign table by eye: ticked rows I, U, p, q, O, 6, S, X; circled 33 wrong cut-outs; moved five boxes of row J to the dash row; questioned h, m, n, o (and wrote d beside o). Applied: circled and questioned boxes marked uncertain, five J boxes to -, one o box to d. Project 699 boxes, 82 types, 169 uncertain; table 528 boxes in 34 rows.

Second pass of the owner's check of the CTTS sign table (528 boxes): ticked 24 rows (I U E A 4 c B Bc d < p q 6 S X 9 C 7 5 b e f y z), circled 13 more cut-outs (now uncertain); not marked: -, <5, w, 2. Project 699 boxes, 82 types, 182 uncertain; table 515 boxes in 34 rows.

Owner's two points applied: the twelve circled P cut-outs are f (stem, top-right loop crossing a lower-left loop); the 7/dash/J sorting by the scribe's alphabet rows (10th sign yod = small flat dash with a short hook, 22nd = tall bar with curl and long diagonal tail): 6 long > boxes to 7, 5 round J hooks to -, 3 old 7 boxes elsewhere, 14 uncertain. The last three a cut-outs (S2L06_5, _21, _22) fixed: one uncertain, one deleted, one split into P and a. Project 699 boxes, 82 types, 179 uncertain; table 518 boxes in 34 rows.

outcome.method_basis: The sign values came from the scribe's own unlabelled alphabet rows (Hebrew order, read left to right as photographed) and the frequent short words פי, יא, מן; the Burda verses then confirmed the key. PGP's content list (which names the Burda verses) was known beforehand; Elbaum's annotated copy was checked only after the key was found.
outcome.notes: About 74% of the non-alphabet cipher signs (302 of 406) read as sense; S1L10 and S1L08 look like letter practice. Elbaum (Princeton Geniza Project) had an unpublished partial key and reading first.

credits.note: Mapped the signs and read parts (alphabet, signature, Burda, legal phrase, an erotic passage); unpublished.

reading_review.note: The Burda verses, date formula, signature, love-poetry line and erotic passage form sentences and are translated; about a quarter of the non-alphabet signs, mostly letter practice, do not.

texts.summary: A practice sheet of Isḥāq the Jew, probably 15th-16th century Egypt: his invented sign alphabet written out twelve times, his signature, verses 1-2 of al-Būṣīrī's Burda, a legal date formula, the word 'thimble', a line of love poetry, 'praise be to God', and an erotic passage in Egyptian colloquial about a woman named Raḥma ending 'my dove, all this is lies'.
